datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) data
datasets.instrument_sensor: REMS Relative Humidity Sensor (RHS); REMS Ground Temperature Sensor (GTS)
datasets.measurement_observable: Air relative humidity with respect to ice (RHi_a) at 1.6 m and air temperature (Ta) from RHS; ground temperature (Tg) derived from infrared radiance from GTS; inferred ground relative humidity (RHi_g and RHl_g) and inferred water vapor pressure (PH2O)
datasets.wavelength_bandpass: GTS infrared bands: 8–14 µm, 15.5–19 µm, and 14.5–15.5 µm
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ meteorological time-series measurements (hourly values derived from 1 Hz sampling); infrared radiance/brightness temperature-derived ground temperature
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: First 1648 sols of MSL mission (landing 5 August 2012); specific sols discussed include 1232 and 1311
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars (landing site coordinates given as 4.7°S, 137°E); along Curiosity traverse; two highlighted points occurred near active sand dunes
datasets.spatial_resolution: GTS field of view covers a ground area of about 100 m^2 (depending on surface-sensor geometry)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Nominal strategy: 5 min of measurements at 1 Hz every Mars hour, with occasional 1–2 hr high-resolution interval mode blocks; analysis uses derived hourly values; GTS averages over 5-min intervals centered at simultaneous RHS measurements
datasets.processing_level_calibration_level: Uses updated calibrations to REMS data (latest calibration referenced as June 2015); analysis further filters to highest-confidence RHS and GTS measurements and uses first 4 s after RHS turn-on
datasets.how_used: Used simultaneous hourly high-confidence RHS (RHi_a, Ta) and GTS-derived ground temperature (Tg) over sols 1–1648 to infer ground relative humidity (RHi_g and RHl_g), compare humidity–temperature conditions against calcium perchlorate phase diagrams, and assess potential surface deliquescence events (including evaluating uncertainty envelopes for sols 1232 and 1311); also used Tg and inferred PH2O for Clausius–Clapeyron (enthalpy) analysis in nighttime 3-hr time spans with data binned over 5 sols.

datasets.pds_dataset_product_name: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) data
datasets.instrument_sensor: REMS (RHS and GTS measurements used to derive water vapor pressure and surface temperature constraints)
datasets.measurement_observable: REMS-derived surface/near-surface humidity/temperature information used to define/fit water vapor pressure just above the regolith and to validate modeled surface temperature and relative humidity
datasets.data_type_product_type: In situ meteorological time-series constraints used as boundary/validation data for a coupled heat and mass transfer (subsurface) model
datasets.acquisition_date_time_range: REMS-derived water vapor pressure fits used to couple boundary condition; model compares simulated surface temperatures and relative humidities with surface-derived REMS values (terrain cases discussed include rover in a low thermal inertia unit between sols 1222 and 1242, Ls ~94°–104°)
datasets.location_coverage: Gale crater, Mars; terrains along MSL traverse (thermal inertia and albedo combinations referenced as occurring along the traverse)
datasets.temporal_resolution_cadence: Model simulates hourly subsurface conditions over one Martian year; boundary condition coupled to REMS-derived water vapor pressure and compared to REMS-derived surface values
datasets.how_used: Used REMS-derived water vapor pressure (fits) as the atmospheric boundary condition at the surface–atmosphere interface for subsurface diffusion modeling, and used REMS-derived surface temperature/relative humidity for validating simulated surface conditions (reported average model errors of ±5 K temperature and ±7% relative humidity relative to REMS).

queries.query: Assemble calibrated, physical-unit meteorological time series from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS humidity and ground-temperature sensors over the early mission in Gale crater (first ~1650 sols) to compute ground-level relative humidity with respect to liquid water and identify pre-dawn windows where calcium-perchlorate deliquescence could be thermodynamically permitted under measurement uncertainty.

Use raw, unprocessed Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS time-series measurements (hourly cadence with short 1 Hz bursts) to isolate the first few seconds after humidity-sensor activation and evaluate sensor self-heating impacts on relative humidity with respect to ice and co-temporal ground-temperature retrievals for brine-stability screening in Gale crater.

final_output.query: Assemble calibrated, physical-unit meteorological time series from the Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS humidity and ground-temperature sensors over the early mission in Gale crater (first ~1650 sols) to compute ground-level relative humidity with respect to liquid water and identify pre-dawn windows where calcium-perchlorate deliquescence could be thermodynamically permitted under measurement uncertainty.

Use raw, unprocessed Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS time-series measurements (hourly cadence with short 1 Hz bursts) to isolate the first few seconds after humidity-sensor activation and evaluate sensor self-heating impacts on relative humidity with respect to ice and co-temporal ground-temperature retrievals for brine-stability screening in Gale crater.

I need raw (EDR) Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS meteorology time series (relative humidity and air/ground temperature) from Gale crater covering the early mission (roughly the first ~1600 sols) to recompute near-surface water vapor pressure and test whether humidity–temperature conditions ever cross deliquescence thresholds relevant to perchlorate brine formation.

I need processed (RDR) Mars Science Laboratory Curiosity REMS environmental products in physical units from Gale crater (including calibrated temperature and humidity) suitable for generating hourly atmospheric boundary-condition fits and validating a coupled heat-and-mass transfer model of shallow subsurface water activity over seasonal to interannual timescales.
